messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: High p99 tail latency observed on /v1/streaming (prod, us-west). SLO impact detected (>5m breach window). Auto-escalation to incidents channel. summary: p95=420ms p99=2.3s, observed streaming stalls and retry storms, ~12% errors 502/504. traced routes: inference-gateway -> controlplane-auth -> config-fetch -> db-token-store.

olivia: ack. I'm oncall. marking incident and starting live triage. who has DB/control-plane context? :hand:

raj: i can take controlplane/auth side. looking at auth token store metrics now.

michelle: i'll tail gateway and streaming logs for stalls and client-side backpressure. grabbing last 30m traces.

olivia: quick customer impact: we have intermittent streaming stalls for some tenants (not full outage). visible as long tails across token refresh calls and config fetch timeouts. recommend temporary mitigation: open a higher-rate window for inference-gateway and enable fallback model routing for streaming endpoints.

raj: auth tokencache p99 latency spiked to 1.8s about ~10:24. error budget at risk. queries to token DB show increased contention and a flurry of short-lived sessions from a single caller IP range. suspicious: bursty client behavior + a recent featureflag rollout that changed refresh cadence.

michelle: logs (gateway):
```
[streaming] 10:25:11.345 GET /v1/streaming id=abc123 tok=xxx status=504 backend=controlplane timeout=1200ms
[streaming] 10:25:12.102 GET /v1/streaming id=def456 tok=yyy status=200 rt=2.1s stall=true
[streaming] 10:26:03.501 retry storm detected for id=abc123 attempts=4
```

olivia: thanks. raj, can you check controlplane->config-fetch metrics and featureflag service? I want to know if config fetches exploded after the flag flip.

raj: running quick queries against controlplane metrics. one-liner:
```
curl -sS 'https://metrics.internal/controlplane?query=rate(config_fetch_requests[5m])' | jq .
```
results show a 6x spike in config_fetch_requests at 10:22-10:26. correlates with featureflag rollout id ff-2026-03 (enabling per-request override caching=false).

dan (via sre-bot): automatic mitigation suggestion: temporarily revert ff-2026-03 for prod, and set controlplane cache TTL back to 60s. also throttle offending client IPs with a rate-window rule.

olivia: proposal for immediate actions (live):
- flip ff-2026-03 -> OFF for prod (dan)
- bump inference-gateway ratewindow for streaming routes to 120r/s for 10m (olivia/raj)
- enable fallback route: route streaming to smaller model variant (reduces config-fetchs) for affected tenants (michelle)
- increase controlplane token DB connection pool temporarily + monitor p99s (raj)

raj: actioning: checking flag toggle endpoint.
```
# dry-run toggle
curl -X POST https://flags.internal/ff-2026-03/toggle -d '{"env":"prod","state":"off"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ME'
```
response: 202 Accepted. pushing change now.

sre-bot: AUTO: feature flag ff-2026-03 rolled back in prod by raj at 10:28 UTC.

michelle: applied fallback route for tenant group A and B to model-small-1 for streaming path (10:29). observed immediate reduction in config_fetch rate from those tenants. tail latency improved for routed sessions: p99 down from 2.3s -> 1.1s.

olivia: good. raj, any change in token DB contention after connection pool bump?

raj: increased pool from 50 -> 120 on prod token-store replica. watching. token latency p99 dropped to 380ms from 1.8s in ~3 minutes. but we still see elevated retries from some clients.

michelle: gateway metrics after mitigation:
- overall p95: 150ms (was 420ms)
- overall p99: 680ms (was 2.3s)
- streaming error rate: 12% -> 3%

olivia: customer impact update: majority of tenants back to nominal, small percentage still seeing tail spikes (likely due to client retry logic). next steps: contact top-5 affected tenants, provide mitigation details.

dan: also recommend adding short-term traffic shaping for the problematic IP range and create an alert to detect featureflag-driven config fetch surges. I'll open a ticket.

raj: noted one trove of repeated refresh tokens from caller app-id=com.partner-x. pushing a temporary rate-limit rule for that app-id to 10r/s.

sre-bot: AUTO: rate-limit rule applied for app-id=com.partner-x by raj at 10:35 UTC.

michelle: follow-up check: some streams still show stalls caused by client-side backoff cycling; will produce a short debug pack for partner-x and ask their SRE to update SDK to exponential backoff + jitter.

olivia: handoff plan: I'm coordinating a 30m post-mortem shadow with platform and applied mitigation owners. oncall handoff to dan in 45m (I will update rota).

raj: logging: captured sample traces and request ids for postmortem. will upload to incident folder.

dan: creating incident artifact and linking runbook steps we executed. also adding checklist to prevent accidental flag rollouts without traffic ramp.

olivia: tl;dr: root cause appears to be a featureflag flip that disabled per-request caching, causing config-fetch storms that amplified auth/token DB contention and produced streaming tail latency and retry storms. live mitigations: rollback flag, gateway ratewindow bump, fallback model routing, token DB pool increase, targeted rate-limiting for offender. customer impact: transient p99 SLO breach, now mostly mitigated. next: postmortem + cadence changes + alerting for config_fetch spikes.

michelle: adding action item for devex: update SDK guidance for token refresh jitter and limit refresh frequency.

olivia: thanks team. I'll escalate to CS for tenant comms and schedule postmortem. closing live incident channel in 1h unless regressions. :white_check_mark:
